conclusion: The current Redis role is broader than disposable runtime memory cache; an in-memory-only replacement would drop real behavior/state.

consumers.name: Generation jobs
consumers.observed: BullMQ Queue/Worker/QueueEvents, job IDs and getState, attempts=3, exponential backoff, retained failures/completions and delayed/priority options
consumers.requiredReplacement: Durable PostgreSQL queue; preserve retries, status/results/events and interrupted-work recovery

consumers.name: Generation results and job mappings
consumers.observed: Redis JSON values with five-minute TTL, queried by status and SSE completion handlers
consumers.requiredReplacement: Owner-scoped result/job mapping with explicit expiry and restart behavior; do not report lost work as success

consumers.name: Schedule read cache and edits
consumers.observed: Read cache is recomputable, but updateSessionSchedule currently writes only Redis and contains a TODO to update the database
consumers.requiredReplacement: Persist user edits transactionally in PostgreSQL before caching; a Map alone would lose edits on restart

consumers.name: Feature usage
consumers.observed: Atomic Redis counters with period expiry; database updates are scheduled asynchronously, and recovery reads PostgreSQL
consumers.requiredReplacement: Authoritative atomic PostgreSQL counter/check-and-increment with period/user/feature identity; no unbounded or stale cached limit decision

consumers.name: Provider limits and cooldown
consumers.observed: Minute/day request counters and cooldown markers with TTL
consumers.requiredReplacement: Bounded process cache for disposable cooldowns; persist applicable quota windows so restarts do not reset provider limits

consumers.name: Socket presence
consumers.observed: Redis sets and socket/user mapping; actual socket objects already held in process memory
consumers.requiredReplacement: Process-owned Map/Set for a single authoritative desktop API; rebuild on reconnect, clear on disconnect, preserve LAN multi-client fan-out

consumers.name: Term/document frequency helper
consumers.observed: Hash increments, document count, pipeline and multi-field reads; no external call site for the legacy EmbeddingGenerator or incrementTermFrequencies was found in the inspected source
consumers.requiredReplacement: Prove unused or migrate persistent corpus statistics to PostgreSQL; do not conflate this helper with the retained multilingual MiniLM service

additionalFindings: The shared Redis abstract connector has a fake fallback that logs writes and returns success without storing data; this cannot count as a working Redis-free implementation.
The current app pins BullMQ 5.49.1; a BullMQ 6 PostgreSQL evaluation does not upgrade the application.

Redis named PUBSUB is used for queue connections; no direct raw Redis publish/subscribe call sites were found in the inspected app source. BullMQ QueueEvents still requires a real replacement event backend.
The retained website/Lambda deployment has direct Redis/BullMQ code and must stay functional while desktop runtime choices are adapted. No Lambda deployment was executed.
